section: Part II, Chapter 31 — The Sabbath as Memorial of Creation
subtitle: דלאלהֵ אלחאירין — The Guide of the Perplexed
author: Moses Maimonides (1138–1204)
intro: Maimonides explains why the Sabbath commandment is enforced with capital punishment and was the cause of a prophet's death: the Sabbath is the third in rank after the existence of God and His unity. Opinions require regular public acts to keep them alive; universal Sabbath rest publicizes creation in time and leads naturally to belief in God. He then explains the apparent discrepancy between the two reasons given in Exodus and Deuteronomy: they address different effects — the honor of the day itself vs. the obligation on Israel — producing a single double blessing for correct belief and bodily rest.

source.edition: Sefaria — version 'Judeo Arabic, Paris, 1856 [jrb]' (the 1856 Paris/Munk Arabic base; public-domain by age)

terms.gloss: the Sabbath — confirming the principle of creation in time
terms.note: Maimonides reads the Sabbath law not primarily as rest but as a weekly public enactment of the doctrine that God created the world in six days — making the theological principle visible.

terms.ja: אלארא אן לם תכן להא אעמאל תת'בתהא
terms.translit: al-ārāʾ in lam takun lahā aʿmāl tuthabbituhā
terms.gloss: opinions without acts to confirm them do not endure
terms.note: A practical principle of Maimonides' philosophy of commandments: beliefs require behavioral reinforcement to survive in the masses.

terms.gloss: two different reasons for two different effects
terms.note: Exodus grounds Sabbath in creation; Deuteronomy grounds it in the Exodus from Egypt. Maimonides harmonizes: Exodus gives the reason for the day's honor; Deuteronomy gives the reason for Israel's specific obligation to rest.

aligned.en: Part Two · Chapter Thirty-One — The Sabbath as Memorial of Creation

aligned.ja: לעלה קד תבין לך אלעלה פי תאכיד שריעהֵ אלסבת וכונהא בסקילה וסיד אלנביין קתל עליהא והי ת'אלת'הֵ וג'וד אלאלאה ונפי אלת'נויה אד' אלנהי ען עבאדהֵ סואה אנמא הו לתקריר אלתוחיד. וקד עלמת מן כלאמי אן אלארא אן לם תכן להא אעמאל תת'בתהא ותשהרהא ותכ'לדהא פי אלג'מהור לם תבק פלד'לך שרענא בתפצ'יל הד'א אליום חתי תת'בת קאעדהֵ חדת' אלעאלם ותשהר פי אלוג'וד אד'א עטל אלנאס כלהם פי יום ואחד פאד'א סיל מא עלהֵ ד'לך כאן אלג'ואב כי ששת ימים עשה י״י.
aligned.en: IT is perhaps clear why the laws concerning Sabbath are so severe, that their transgression is visited with death by stoning, and that the greatest of the prophets put a person to death for breaking the Sabbath. The commandment of the Sabbath is the third from the commandment concerning the existence and the unity of God. For the commandment not to worship any other being is merely an explanation of the first. You know already from what I have said, that no opinions retain their vitality except those which are confirmed, published, and by certain actions constantly revived among the people. Therefore we are told in the Law to honour this day; in order to confirm thereby the principle of Creation which will spread in the world, when all peoples keep Sabbath on the same day. For when the question is asked, why this is done, the answer is given: "For in six days the Lord hath made," etc. (Exod. 20:11).

aligned.ja: וקד ג'א פי הד'ה אלשריעה עלתאן מכ'תלפתאן לאנהמא למעלולין מכ'תלפין וד'לך אנה קאל פי עלהֵ תעט'ים אלסבת פי עשר הדברות אלאולי קאל כי ששת ימים עשה י״י וגו' וקאל פי משנה תורה וזכרת כי עבד היית במצרים על כן צוך י״י אלהיך לעשות את יום השבת והד'א צחיח לאן אלמעלול פי אלקול אלאול הו תשריף אליום ותעט'ימה כמא קאל על כן ברך י״י את יום השבת ויקדשהו הד'א הו אלמעלול אלתאבע לעלהֵ כי ששת ימים וגו' אמא תשריענא בה ואמרנא נחן בחפט'ה פהו מעלול תאבע לעלהֵ כוננא עבדים במצרים אלד'י לם נכן נכ'דם באכ'תיארנא ומתי שינא ולא נסתטיע אלעטלה
aligned.en: Two different reasons are given for this commandment, because of two different objects. In the Decalogue in Exodus, the following reason is given for distinguishing the Sabbath: "For in six days," etc. But in Deuteronomy (chap. 5:15) the reason is given: "And thou shalt remember that thou hast been a slave in the land of Egypt, etc., therefore the Lord thy God commanded thee," etc. This difference can easily be explained. In the former, the cause of the honour and distinction of the day is given; comp. "Therefore the Lord hath blessed the day of the Sabbath and sanctified it" (Exod. 20:10), and the cause for this is, "For in six days," etc. But the fact that God has given us the law of the Sabbath and commanded us to keep it, is the consequence of our having been slaves; for then our work did not depend on our will, nor could we choose the time for it; and we could not rest.

pairs.ja: ג'א פי הד'ה אלשריעה עלתאן מכ'תלפתאן לאנהמא למעלולין מכ'תלפין
pairs.en: Two different reasons are given for this commandment, because of two different objects

pairs.ja: אלמעלול פי אלקול אלאול הו תשריף אליום ותעט'ימה
pairs.en: In the former, the cause of the honour and distinction of the day is given

pairs.ja: תשריענא בה ואמרנא נחן בחפט'ה פהו מעלול תאבע לעלהֵ כוננא עבדים במצרים
pairs.en: the fact that God has given us the law of the Sabbath and commanded us to keep it, is the consequence of our having been slaves

aligned.ja: פשרענא באלעטלה ואלראחה לנג'מע אלאמרין אעתקאד ראי צחיח והו חדת' אלעאלם אלדאל עלי וג'וד אלאלאה באול כ'אטר ואסהל נט'ר ותד'כר אפצ'אל אללה עלינא פי אראחתנא מתחת סבלות מצרים פכאנה אפצ'אל עאם פי צחיח אלראי אלנט'רי וצלאח אלחאל אלג'סמאני:
aligned.en: Thus God commanded us to abstain from work on the Sabbath, and to rest, for two purposes; namely, (1) That we might confirm the true theory, that of the Creation, which at once and clearly leads to the theory of the existence of God. (2) That we might remember how kind God has been in freeing us from the burden of the Egyptians.—The Sabbath is therefore a double blessing: it gives us correct notions, and also promotes the well-being of our bodies.

pairs.en: God commanded us to abstain from work on the Sabbath, and to rest, for two purposes

pairs.ja: אעתקאד ראי צחיח והו חדת' אלעאלם אלדאל עלי וג'וד אלאלאה
pairs.en: That we might confirm the true theory, that of the Creation, which at once and clearly leads to the theory of the existence of God

pairs.ja: תד'כר אפצ'אל אללה עלינא פי אראחתנא מתחת סבלות מצרים
pairs.en: That we might remember how kind God has been in freeing us from the burden of the Egyptians

pairs.ja: פכאנה אפצ'אל עאם פי צחיח אלראי אלנט'רי וצלאח אלחאל אלג'סמאני
pairs.en: The Sabbath is therefore a double blessing: it gives us correct notions, and also promotes the well-being of our bodies
